10031532:
Testimony of the Maine Municipal Association
Neither for Nor Against
LD 123- An Act Regarding Licensure of Emergency Medical Service Persons
January 28, 2024
_____________________________________________________________________________________
Sen. Bailey, Rep. Matheson and distinguished members of the Health Coverage, Insurance and Financial Services Committee, my name is Rebecca Graham, and I am submitting placed holder testimony on behalf of Maine Municipal Association for LD 123, An Act Regarding Licensure of Emergency Medical Service Persons. The positions the association provides are at the direction of our 70 member Legislative Police Committee (LPC) who have not had the opportunity to vet the potential impacts of this bill, but are meeting this Thursday, January 30, to develop their official position. If the committee has held a work session on the bill prior to the development of MMA's official position, I will submit additional testimony following this meeting.
As the committee reviews the potential impacts of a seemingly small language change, it may be worth understanding that in many areas of the state, municipal ambulance services have been challenged to find training for community members who desire to serve their ambulance service, often in a part time capacity. In rural communities, the part-time model for staffing is crucial to guarantee an ambulance response when the calls for service regionally are far below a sustainable level for full time staffing. Some communities have even rented apartments to provide per diem employees an opportunity to serve far away from their home and protect a 5 minute response time model while also providing experience for new emergency medical technicians often necessary to work for a larger community.
During regional meetings held with MMA this fall, northern communities shared their challenges with accessing EMT training, due to a lack of qualified instruction during appropriate hours and distances to their municipalities. Despite having ample volunteers who desired to receive the training and serve, and satellite community college and University spaces, these communities were instead challenged by training offerings that were only held during the day, and over an hour away, excluding access for individuals who held other jobs in the community to become certified. If the language change proposed by the department in LD 123 from "practical exam" to "assessment" further makes certification training harder to access or deliver, this will not be a change our most vulnerable rural communities will welcome.
Conversely, if the language change enables the EMS Board to broaden the ways individuals can meet certification requirements in the field with experienced staff, the change will likely be welcomed. I will submit the official position of the Association following our LPC deliberation on the language Thursday. Thank you in advance for your careful consideration and service to Maine's communities.
183113:
Scott Cyrway
Senator, District I6

132nd MAINE SENATE

3 State House Station
Augusta, ME 04333

Senator Bailey, Representative Mathieson, and the esteemed members of the Health
Coverage, Insurance, and Financial Services Committee,
I am here today to present LD 123, "An Act Regarding Licensure of Emergency Medical
Services Persons." This bill replaces the requirement that a person must complete a practical evaluation of emergency medical treatment skills to be licensed with a requirement that they must complete an assessment of emergency medical treatment skills approved by the Emergency Medical Services' Board. The bill before you updates Maine's lagging standards, bringing them
into conformity with the model supported by the National Registry of EMTs. In my
conversations with Joe Kellner, the Chief Executive Officer of LifeFlight of Maine, he noted that
"The correlation between the old testing model and success in the field is unknown but
subjectively limited. We know the new method does well at predicting success, is well proven
and widely accepted."
During this hearing, you will hear why the bill before you is necessary, from the
organizations it will impact most. I hope you agree with us and ask you to vote ought to pass.
Thank you for your time.
10031292:
Valerie Caruso Augusta LD 123
Licensure of emergency personnel is a critical topic that ensures the safety and well-being of individuals in need of urgent medical attention. The process of obtaining licensure for emergency personnel involves rigorous training, education, and testing to guarantee that individuals are capable and qualified to respond to emergencies effectively.
Having proper licensure in place not only ensures that emergency personnel have the necessary skills and knowledge to handle a wide range of medical situations, but also gives peace of mind to patients and their families. Knowing that the individuals responding to their emergency are licensed and trained professionals can help alleviate anxiety and instill confidence in the care being provided.
Overall, licensure of emergency personnel is a vital component of the healthcare system that plays a crucial role in safeguarding the health and well-being of individuals in emergency situations. The process ensures that only qualified individuals are allowed to provide care, ultimately leading to better outcomes for patients and a higher standard of emergency response. It is important to continue to support and uphold licensure requirements for emergency personnel to maintain a high level of quality care in emergency situations.
183114:
Testimony of William O'Neal
Director, Maine Bureau of Emergency Medical Services (Maine EMS)
Department of Public Safety
IN SUPPORT of LD 123
"An Act Regarding Licensure of Emergency Medical Services Persons"
Presented by Senator Cyrway of Kennebec
BEFORE THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON HEALTH COVERAGE, INSURANCE AND FINANCIAL
SERVICES
Work Session: Tuesday, January 28, 2025
Senator Bailey, Representative Mathieson, and honorable members of the joint standing committee on
Health Coverage, Insurance and Financial Services:
My name is Wil O'NeaI, and I am the Director of Maine Emergency Medical Services (Maine EMS) lam testifying on behalf of the Maine Department of Public Safety and Maine EMS in support of "An Act
Regarding Licensure of Emergency Medical Services Persons"
In Maine, we previously used a practical evaluation (a checklist) to gauge student competency at the end of an EMS training program. Our national certifying body, The National Registry of Emergency
Medical Technicians (NREMT) saw through national education standard changes, data, and feedback that this checklist approach no longer met the needs of our students or the demands of the 21"~century
workforce. NREMT responded by establishing the new psychomotor competency portfolio (Portfolio) assessment standard for EMS Education. "Competency of psychomotor skills is not possessed after one
successful demonstration of a particular skill. Competency requires repeated student skill demonstrations (practice) until the demonstration of that skill can be automatically delivered during
stressful times, in unfamiliar places and to patients who are severely ill or injured." (2015, NREMT
Paramedic Psychomotor Competency Portfolio)
In 2023, the Maine EMS Board allowed the option of the new portfolio assessment at the EMT and EMR level, and ALL Maine EMS training centers have since transitioned away from the practical evaluation to the new portfolio assessment standard.
Since the change from the practical evaluation to the new portfolio standard, Maine EMS Training
Centers report an increase in National Registry pass rates, a decrease in cost per student, and the removal of scheduling separate evaluations, an administrative burden which could take months after course completion.
By adopting the change in language from the practical evaluation to the Portfolio Assessment standard in
our statute, this bill works to establish a more effective and future-ready EMS education system for the next generation of EMS professionals in Maine.
Thank you, I am more than happy to answer any questions you may have.
